claim: Naive session grouping by raw connection_id fragments every schema-mixed session into two disjoint halves; canonical_session_id derived from event_id prefix produces the correct 62,515-session count instead of 125,030.
proves: Shows that connection_id alone is not a valid session key across schema_version 1 and 2.
does_not_prove: Does not prove every session in the replay contains a schema-mixed pair; confirmed only by full-dataset count comparison.
alternative_considered: Trusting connection_id as documented in replay-interface.json - rejected after producing 125,030 sessions against the verified true count of 62,515.
disposition: Used event_id-derived canonical_session_id for all downstream sessionization, clustering, and hashing stages.

claim: CLUSTER-001 (3 source IPs: 198.51.100.155, 198.51.100.160, 198.51.100.87) share an identical set of 4 payload hashes, distinguishing it from 248 other source IPs with no payload activity.
proves: Shows shared payload distribution infrastructure across exactly 3 IPs, not inferred from reputation.
does_not_prove: Does not prove real-world actor identity - source IPs are RFC 5737 documentation-range test addresses in this replay.
alternative_considered: Clustering by credential_fingerprint or protocol targeting - rejected, both signals are near-universal across ~251-252 of 252 source IPs and carry no discriminating value.
disposition: Used payload_sha256 co-occurrence as the sole clustering signal; credential/protocol universality recorded as context only.

claim: Payload hash e1c27bf70abbabeb9ee71bffa8f9737b70361802170cbe39c11bbdc42875263f was downloaded 73 times with the declared bytes field varying across every occurrence, making bytes unreliable as a payload-size indicator.
proves: Shows the bytes field cannot be treated as authoritative payload size for this hash.
does_not_prove: Does not prove bytes is unreliable for hashes outside this dataset or outside this pipeline's normalization.
alternative_considered: Treating bytes as ground-truth file size in the STIX File object - rejected once inconsistency was found; flagged bytes_is_unreliable=true on every affected row instead.
disposition: Every hash-ledger.csv row for an inconsistent hash carries an explicit note; STIX indicator description states the same limitation.

claim: Session S-ed7d82-0000211 contains the shared evidence marker UBI-A6-SHARED-B1 on a command event running uname -a && id, one second before a payload_download from the same session.
proves: Shows a command-level, evidence-marker-linked session with a direct recon-to-download sequence.
does_not_prove: Does not prove the operator was human vs. scripted from this session alone - see session-analysis.md Intent assessment.
alternative_considered: Treating the auth_success credential in this session as attacker-specific - rejected, this credential fingerprint is shared across ~251 other source IPs.
disposition: Full evidence chain, ATT&CK mapping, and confidence-graded interpretation recorded in session-analysis.md.

claim: The STIX 2.1 bundle contains 4 hash indicators, 1 infrastructure object (CLUSTER-001), 4 indicates relationships, and 1 note carrying the evidence marker locator - 11 objects total, deterministically generated.
proves: Shows STIX objects are generated only for the high-confidence cluster, not for background/reconnaissance-only IPs.
does_not_prove: Does not prove threat-intel accuracy beyond what this replay's own evidence supports - no external reputation lookups were performed.
alternative_considered: Elevating all three clusters (including background and reconnaissance-only) to STIX Indicators - rejected, would imply actionable attribution for noise.
disposition: STIX object IDs are content-derived (uuid5), confirmed byte-identical across two independent pipeline runs (test_reproducibility.py).

claim: Running the full analysis pipeline twice against the same replay file produces byte-identical clusters.json, hash-ledger.csv, hash-summary.json, stix-bundle.json, all three detection files, and sessions.parquet.
exact_locator: stdout: 'All outputs reproducible across two clean runs.'
proves: Shows the mandatory analysis pipeline is deterministic, satisfying the clean-state rebuild requirement.
does_not_prove: Does not prove the sensor-infrastructure boundary is equally reproducible - that is evidenced separately in isolation-results.json.
alternative_considered: Relying on visual inspection of two runs instead of an automated byte-comparison - rejected in favor of an explicit script-based check.
disposition: test_reproducibility.py retained in tests/ as a standing, rerunnable proof, not a one-time manual check.

claim: Isolation tests ISO-01 through ISO-06 and ISO-08 all PASS against the provisioned sensor boundary from management, external, and sensor viewpoints; ISO-07 is recorded NOT_ATTEMPTED as an explicitly out-of-scope optional live-exposure test.
proves: Shows the fail-closed boundary correctly allows only declared management access and denies RFC1918, metadata, and unapproved external access, while allowing required DNS egress.
does_not_prove: Does not prove ISO-07 (internet-to-honeypot reachability), which requires genuine public exposure and was deliberately scoped to the optional live-sensor task.
alternative_considered: Attempting ISO-07 against a private/lab network - rejected, would produce a misleading result since it would not test genuine internet reachability.
disposition: isolation_runner.py generates results directly from isolation-tests.csv as the template, filling only measured fields.
